text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD

- Bank Bawag considers acquiring a 49 percent stake in state-owned postal savings bank PSK, as is cooperative banking group Raiffeisen. Both say they are not interested in taking over GiroCredit bank.
- Austria's tourism industry will stabilise this year after years of decline, economic analysts say.

- Former finance minister Ferdinand Lacina, currently head of GiroCredit, may become Creditanstalt's next chief executive following majority-takeover through Bank Austria. Current board members of Bank Austria are also being mentioned as possible candidates.
- Investment group Kapital & Wert plans to take over electronics retailer Niedermayer.

- Social Democrat party manager Brigitte Ederer says a rift in the coalition government of Social Democrats and conservative People's Party over the sale of Creditanstalt is likely to leave some scars.
- Sports goods maker HTM is suddenly prepared to repay 156 million schillings in overdue loans if banks in return would agree to keep all credit lines open.
- Technology group VA Tech plans to introduce a strategy aimed at increasing shareholder value.
DIE PRESSE
- Small shareholders of Creditanstalt plan to take legal action against Bank Austria's takeover of Creditanstalt, saying Bank Austria's cash offer was insufficient.
- Bawag and its majority shareholder, Germany's Bayerische Landesbank, are interested in taking over GiroCredit.
- Austria is at the top of a list of most favoured nations for investments abroad by German companies.
- The far-right Freedom Party says it remains open to talks with the conservatives.
KURIER
- After only just having been introduced at the start of the year, a new fee on health services may be scrapped as its administration cost exceed projected revenues.
- Social Democrats and People's Party say they want to end their differences over the sale of Creditanstalt, but the next stumbling blocks for the uneasy coalition are already on the horizon.
- AVZ, the City of Vienna's foundation which owns a major stake in both Bank Austria and GiroCredit, may make a loss if it has to sell its GiroCredit stake.
- Customers of Creditanstalt say they will not be affected by the acquisition of a majority stake in the bank by rival Bank Austria.
SALZBURGER NACHRICHTEN
- Creditanstalt wants to retain small stakes in communal financing bank Investkredit and government financing agent Kontrollbank.
WIRTSCHAFTSBLATT
- Creditanstalt preferred shares slump four percent on Wednesday, traders say investors are disappointed about the effects of bank's takeover through Bank Austria.
